claim: Thylakoid membranes scaffold an assortment of large protein complexes that work together to harness the energy of light.
source: Thylakoid membranes scaffold an assortment of large protein complexes that work together to harness the energy of light.
evidence: This is a general statement about thylakoid membrane function that draws from established scientific knowledge about photosynthesis.

claim: The authors previously used in situ cryo-electron tomography to reveal the native architecture of thylakoid membranes.
source: Previously, we used in situ cryo-electron tomography to reveal the native architecture of thylakoid membranes (Engel et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: The authors developed a new method to visualize membrane surface topology.
source: Combined with a new method to visualize membrane surface topology, we map the molecular landscapes of thylakoid membranes inside green algae cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes the development and application of membranograms as a new visualization method.

claim: Photosystems I and II are strictly segregated at the borders between appressed and non-appressed membrane domains.
source: Our tomograms provide insights into the molecular forces that drive thylakoid stacking and reveal that photosystems I and II are strictly segregated at the borders between appressed and non-appressed membrane domains.
evidence: This claim is supported by tomographic data and membranogram analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Membranes can organize their embedded proteins into specialized domains, concentrating molecular partners together to drive biological processes.
source: In addition to compartmentalizing the cell into organelles, membranes can organize their embedded proteins into specialized domains, concentrating molecular partners together to drive biological processes (Malinsky et al., 2013; Case et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Thylakoids are sheet-like membrane-bound compartments that produce oxygen while converting light energy into biochemical energy.
source: The question of membrane domain organization is especially pertinent to thylakoids, sheet-like membrane-bound compartments that produce oxygen while converting light energy into biochemical energy, thereby sustaining most of the life on Earth.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about thylakoid function.

claim: Four large protein complexes within the thylakoid membrane drive light-dependent photosynthetic reactions.
source: These light-dependent photosynthetic reactions are driven by the concerted actions of four large protein complexes within the thylakoid membrane.
evidence: This is established knowledge about photosynthetic machinery.

claim: Photosystem II (PSII), cytochrome b6f (cytb6f), and photosystem I (PSI) form an electron transport chain that produces NADPH and pumps protons into the thylakoid lumen.
source: Photosystem II (PSII), cytochrome b6f (cytb6f), and photosystem I (PSI) form an electron transport chain that produces NADPH and pumps protons into the thylakoid lumen.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the photosynthetic electron transport chain.

claim: ATP synthase uses the electrochemical gradient across the membrane to generate ATP.
source: ATP synthase then uses this electrochemical gradient across the membrane to generate ATP.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ATP synthase function.

claim: In most photosynthetic eukaryotes, thylakoid membranes are subdivided into appressed regions that face adjacent membranes within thylakoid stacks and non-appressed regions that freely face the stroma.
source: In most photosynthetic eukaryotes, the thylakoid membranes are subdivided into appressed regions that face adjacent membranes within thylakoid stacks (called grana in higher plants) and non-appressed regions that freely face the stroma (Austin and Staehelin, 2011; Nevo et al., 2012; Pribil et al., 2014; Engel et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: In both plants and algae, PSII and PSI appear to be segregated to the appressed and non-appressed membranes, respectively.
source: In both plants and algae, PSII and PSI appear to be segregated to the appressed and non-appressed membranes, respectively (Goodenough and Staehelin, 1971; Wollman et al., 1980; Pribil et al., 2014; Flori et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lateral heterogeneity is believed to coordinate photosynthesis by concentrating different reactions within specialized membrane domains.
source: This lateral heterogeneity is believed to coordinate photosynthesis by concentrating different reactions within specialized membrane domains, while the redistribution of light-harvesting complex II (LHCII) antennas between these domains may enable adaptation to changing environmental conditions (Minagawa and Tokutsu, 2015; Nawrocki et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and represents a hypothesis in the field.

claim: Freeze-fracture electron microscopy provides views of membrane-embedded protein complexes within the cell.
source: Much of what is known about the molecular organization of thylakoids comes from freeze-fracture electron microscopy (and the related deep etch technique), which provides views of membrane-embedded protein complexes within the cell (Heuser, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation describing the technique.

claim: Freeze-fracture electron microscopy combined with biochemical fractionation helped describe the lateral heterogeneity of thylakoids.
source: Combined with biochemical fractionation (Andersson and Anderson, 1980; Albertsson, 2001), these membrane panoramas helped describe the lateral heterogeneity of thylakoids (Goodenough and Staehelin, 1971; Staehelin, 1976; Olive et al., 1979; Wollman et al., 1980; Staehelin and Arntzen, 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Platinum replicas produced by freeze-fracture have limited resolution and only provide access to random fracture planes through the membranes.
source: However, the platinum replicas produced by this technique have limited resolution and only provide access to random fracture planes through the membranes.
evidence: This is a known limitation of the freeze-fracture technique.

claim: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) has been used to map the macromolecular organization of thylakoids.
source: More recently, atomic force microscopy (AFM) has been used to map the macromolecular organization of thylakoids (Sznee et al., 2011; Johnson et al., 2014; Wood et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous AFM studies.

claim: AFM can distinguish between each of the major photosynthetic complexes within a hydrated membrane.
source: AFM can very precisely measure topology and thus, can distinguish between each of the major photosynthetic complexes within a hydrated membrane.
evidence: This is a known capability of AFM based on cited literature.

claim: For AFM, membranes must first be removed from the cell, and only one membrane surface can be visualized at a time.
source: However, the membranes must first be removed from the cell, and only one membrane surface can be visualized at a time.
evidence: This is a known limitation of AFM technique.

claim: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) has been shown to resolve PSII complexes within hydrated thylakoids.
source: As an alternative, cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) has been shown to resolve PSII complexes within hydrated thylakoids (Daum et al., 2010; Kouřil et al., 2011; Levitan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous cryo-ET studies.

claim: In previous cryo-ET studies, thylakoids were isolated from the chloroplast in order to produce sufficiently thin samples.
source: Although multiple overlapping membranes can be imaged with this technique, the thylakoids in these studies were isolated from the chloroplast in order to produce sufficiently thin samples.
evidence: This describes a limitation of previous cryo-ET studies based on cited literature.

claim: The authors combined cryo-focused ion beam milling with cryo-ET to image thylakoid membranes within vitreously-frozen Chlamydomonas reinhardtii cells.
source: In pursuit of this goal, we combined cryo-focused ion beam milling (Marko et al., 2007; Schaffer et al., 2017) with cryo-ET (Asano et al., 2016) to image thylakoid membranes within vitreously-frozen Chlamydomonas reinhardtii cells.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study, supported by citations.

claim: Several years ago, the authors demonstrated how their approach can capture the undisturbed membrane architecture of Chlamydomonas, revealing an elaborate system of stacked thylakoids.
source: Several years ago, we demonstrated how this approach can capture the undisturbed membrane architecture of this green alga, revealing an elaborate system of stacked thylakoids (Engel et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The previous investigation was limited to a description of membrane architecture due to lower resolution of CCD cameras used at that time.
source: However, due to the lower resolution of the CCD cameras used at that time, this investigation was limited to a description of membrane architecture, without visualizing the protein complexes embedded within these membranes.
evidence: This describes a limitation of the previous study.

claim: The authors leverage advances in direct detector cameras and the Volta phase plate to resolve thylakoid-embedded complexes.
source: Here, we leverage advances in direct detector cameras and the contrast-enhancing Volta phase plate (Danev et al., 2014) to resolve the thylakoid-embedded complexes, enabling us to describe the molecular organization of thylakoids in situ, within their native cellular context.
evidence: This describes the technical advances used in the current study.

claim: The tomograms show numerous densities corresponding to ribosomes and photosynthetic complexes decorating the appressed and non-appressed surfaces of the thylakoid network.
source: Our tomograms show numerous densities corresponding to ribosomes and photosynthetic complexes decorating the appressed and non-appressed surfaces of the thylakoid network (Figure 1A–B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by tomographic data shown in figures and videos.

claim: Close visual inspection revealed the unmistakable shapes of ATP synthase and PSII protruding into the stroma and lumen, respectively.
source: Close visual inspection revealed the unmistakable shapes of ATP synthase and PSII protruding into the stroma and lumen, respectively (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by visual inspection of tomographic data shown in figures.

claim: The authors developed a visualization approach called a 'membranogram', where densities from the tomogram are projected onto the surface of a segmented membrane.
source: In order to map these decorating densities into the native thylakoid architecture, we developed a visualization approach called a 'membranogram', where densities from the tomogram are projected onto the surface of a segmented membrane (Figure 1E).
evidence: This describes the development of a new method, demonstrated in the figures.

claim: Membranograms produce a topological view of the membrane surface that resembles AFM data.
source: The result is a topological view of the membrane surface that resembles AFM data.
evidence: This is a comparison based on the characteristics of the membranogram output.

claim: Unlike AFM, membranograms can display the topology of both sides of each membrane within the cellular volume.
source: However, unlike AFM, membranograms can display the topology of both sides of each membrane within the cellular volume.
evidence: This describes an advantage of membranograms over AFM.

claim: Membranograms allow tracking of how densities change as they extend from the membrane surface.
source: By dynamically growing and shrinking the segmentations, the membranograms allow us to track how densities change as they extend from the membrane surface and compare these densities to mapped in molecular models of different complexes (Video 2).
evidence: This describes a capability of the membranogram method demonstrated in the video.

claim: Manual assignment of thylakoid-associated complexes was enabled by considering whether the densities projected into the stroma or thylakoid lumen and comparing the densities to known structures of each complex.
source: This enabled the manual assignment of thylakoid-associated complexes by considering whether the densities projected into the stroma or thylakoid lumen (Figure 2A) and then comparing the densities to known structures of each complex (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the methodology for particle identification.

claim: The authors used manually picked positions to generate subtomogram averages of PSII and ATP synthase, structurally confirming that membranograms can correctly identify these complexes.
source: We used manually picked positions to generate subtomogram averages of PSII and ATP synthase, structurally confirming that membranograms can correctly identify these complexes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by subtomogram averaging data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The authors quantified 84 membrane regions from four tomograms.
source: In total, we quantified 84 membrane regions from four tomograms (Table 1) and found clear evidence of lateral heterogeneity: PSII was almost exclusively found in the appressed regions, whereas PSI, ATP synthase, and ribosomes were restricted to the non-appressed regions.
evidence: This describes the quantitative analysis performed, with data shown in Table 1.

claim: PSII was almost exclusively found in the appressed regions.
source: In total, we quantified 84 membrane regions from four tomograms (Table 1) and found clear evidence of lateral heterogeneity: PSII was almost exclusively found in the appressed regions, whereas PSI, ATP synthase, and ribosomes were restricted to the non-appressed regions.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from 84 membrane regions shown in Table 1.

claim: PSI, ATP synthase, and ribosomes were restricted to the non-appressed regions.
source: In total, we quantified 84 membrane regions from four tomograms (Table 1) and found clear evidence of lateral heterogeneity: PSII was almost exclusively found in the appressed regions, whereas PSI, ATP synthase, and ribosomes were restricted to the non-appressed regions.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from 84 membrane regions shown in Table 1.

claim: Cytb6f was observed with almost equal abundance in both appressed and non-appressed regions.
source: Cytb6f was observed with almost equal abundance in both regions, with the caveat that we had lower confidence in our assignment of this complex in non-appressed membranes.
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative observations with a noted limitation.

claim: Poly-ribosome chains were clearly resolved decorating the non-appressed thylakoids.
source: Poly-ribosome chains were clearly resolved decorating the non-appressed thylakoids (Figures 1A and 2C–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by visual data shown in multiple figures.

claim: PSI, PSII, cytb6f, and ATP synthase were distributed relatively evenly along their respective membrane regions.
source: In contrast, PSI, PSII, cytb6f, and ATP synthase were distributed relatively evenly along their respective membrane regions (nearest-neighbor distances plotted in Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by nearest-neighbor distance analysis shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The concentrations measured for different photosynthetic complexes were similar to previous biochemical estimates.
source: The concentrations we measured for different photosynthetic complexes were similar to previous biochemical estimates (Allred and Staehelin, 1986; Vallon et al., 1991; Albertsson, 2001) as well as AFM measurements (Johnson et al., 2014) and counts of 'membrane-embedded particles' from freeze-fracture (Wollman et al., 1980; Staehelin, 2003), indicating that direct comparisons can be made between cryo-ET data and these earlier studies.
evidence: This claim compares the current data to previous studies cited in the text.

claim: The concentration of PSII dimers observed in appressed regions (1122 particles/μm2) was in agreement with previous freeze-fracture measurements from Chlamydomonas (1250 particles/μm2).
source: In particular, the concentration of PSII dimers that we observed in appressed regions (1122 particles/μm2) was in agreement with previous freeze-fracture measurements from Chlamydomonas (1250 particles/μm2) (Wollman et al., 1980).
evidence: This claim compares quantitative measurements to a cited previous study.

claim: Very few PSII complexes were observed in the non-appressed membranes.
source: We observed very few PSII complexes in the non-appressed membranes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), but it remains to be tested whether different conditions, such as damaging high light intensities, may increase the abundance of PSII outside the appressed domains.
evidence: This claim is supported by observations shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The observation that cytb6f is distributed relatively evenly between appressed and non-appressed membranes is consistent with previous reports.
source: Our observation that cytb6f is distributed relatively evenly between appressed and non-appressed membranes is also consistent with previous reports, although this ratio varies widely in the literature and may be modulated by physiological conditions (Vallon et al., 1991; Staehelin, 2003; Kirchhoff et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim compares observations to previous literature with citations.

claim: The total number of densities counted on non-appressed membranes (4907 particles/μm2) was similar to the number of particles previously observed by freeze-fracture in Chlamydomonas (4500 particles/μm2).
source: The total number of densities that we counted on non-appressed membranes (4907 particles/μm2) was similar to the number of particles previously observed by freeze-fracture in Chlamydomonas (4500 particles/μm2) (Wollman et al., 1980).
evidence: This claim compares quantitative measurements to a cited previous study.

claim: The authors measured a PSII/PSI monomer ratio of 2.1 by cryo-ET.
source: Spectroscopic estimates for the stoichiometry of PSII/PSI monomers in thylakoids vary widely from 0.8 to 2.1 (Danielsson et al., 2004; Fan et al., 2007); by cryo-ET, we measured a PSII/PSI monomer ratio of 2.1, but we note that PSI was not identified with high confidence (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative measurements with a noted limitation about confidence.

claim: The concentration of ATP synthase measured on non-appressed membranes (1652 particles/μm2) was very similar to previous cryo-ET analysis of isolated spinach thylakoids (1770 particles/μm2).
source: The concentration of ATP synthase that we measured on non-appressed membranes (1652 particles/μm2) was very similar to previous cryo-ET analysis of isolated spinach thylakoids (1770 particles/μm2) (Daum et al., 2010) but more than twice the concentration initially proposed from freeze-fracture (710 particles/μm2) (Miller and Staehelin, 1976; Staehelin, 2003).
evidence: This claim compares quantitative measurements to cited previous studies.

claim: At the boundary between the appressed and non-appressed membranes of higher plants, it is widely believed that there is a specialized domain called the 'grana margin' where PSII and PSI intermix.
source: At the boundary between the appressed and non-appressed membranes of higher plants (i.e., the grana and stroma lamellae), it is widely believed that there is a specialized domain called the 'grana margin' where PSII and PSI intermix (Anderson, 1989; Wollenberger et al., 1995; Kitmitto et al., 1997; Albertsson, 2001).
evidence: This claim describes a hypothesis in the field supported by citations.

claim: The authors observed a sharp boundary between PSII and PSI that exactly matched the division in thylakoid architecture.
source: Using membranograms, we visualized the molecular organization of native thylakoids that transitioned between appressed and non-appressed regions (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1). Strikingly, we observed a sharp boundary between PSII and PSI that exactly matched the division in thylakoid architecture.
evidence: This claim is supported by membranogram data shown in the figures.

claim: The photosystems did not intermix, and there was no clear difference in particle abundance near the boundary.
source: The photosystems did not intermix, and we saw no clear difference in particle abundance near the boundary.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from membranogram analysis.

claim: The authors find no evidence for 'grana margins' in Chlamydomonas cells grown under mixotrophic growth in moderate light conditions.
source: We therefore find no evidence for 'grana margins' in Chlamydomonas cells grown under these conditions (mixotrophic growth in moderate light, see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the absence of observed intermixing in the data.

claim: PSI is presumably excluded from appressed membranes because its ~3 nm stromal density is too bulky to fit into the ~3 nm space between stacked thylakoids.
source: What drives the strict lateral heterogeneity that we observe between appressed and non-appressed domains? PSI is presumably excluded from appressed membranes because its ~3 nm stromal density is too bulky to fit into the ~3 nm space between stacked thylakoids (Daum et al., 2010; Kirchhoff et al., 2011; Engel et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on structural constraints, supported by citations.

claim: PSII and its associated LHCII antennas may induce thylakoid stacking, a causal relationship that would precisely limit PSII to appressed membranes.
source: Conversely, PSII and its associated LHCII antennas may induce thylakoid stacking, a causal relationship that would precisely limit PSII to appressed membranes.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about the mechanism of thylakoid stacking.

claim: Several studies have observed semi-crystalline arrays of C2S2-type or C2S2M2-type PSII-LHCII supercomplexes in thylakoids isolated from higher plants.
source: Several studies have observed semi-crystalline arrays of C2S2-type (Boekema et al., 2000; Daum et al., 2010) or C2S2M2-type (Kouřil et al., 2012) PSII-LHCII supercomplexes in thylakoids isolated from higher plants, and it has been proposed that the overlap of LHCII or PSII between membranes mediates thylakoid stacking (McDonnel and Staehelin, 1980; Boekema et al., 2000; Standfuss et al., 2005; Daum et al., 2010; Albanese et al., 2017; Albanese et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The authors observed randomly oriented PSII complexes instead of ordered arrays.
source: Although we observed randomly oriented PSII complexes instead of ordered arrays, we nonetheless looked for evidence of supercomplex interactions across native thylakoid stacks (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the tomographic data.

claim: The authors observed a ~3% in-plane overlap between C2S2M2L2-type supercomplex models.
source: While the majority of C2S2M2L2-type supercomplexes fit within the plane of the membrane, we observed a ~3% in-plane overlap between the models (Figure 4C), indicating that some PSII may form smaller supercomplexes under the moderate light conditions that we examined (~90 µmol photons m−2s−1).
evidence: This claim is based on modeling analysis shown in the figure.

claim: There is ample space within the appressed regions of Chlamydomonas thylakoids to accommodate large PSII-LHCII supercomplexes.
source: Nevertheless, we observed that there is ample space within the appressed regions of Chlamydomonas thylakoids to accommodate large PSII-LHCII supercomplexes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the modeling analysis of supercomplex placement.

claim: Mapping in C2S2M2-type supercomplexes resulted in almost no in-plane overlap between the models.
source: Mapping in C2S2M2-type supercomplexes, a slightly smaller arrangement that has been purified from higher plants (Su et al., 2017; van Bezouwen et al., 2017), resulted in almost no in-plane overlap between the models.
evidence: This claim is based on modeling analysis with cited structures.

claim: Supercomplex models of different sizes occupied 47.3 ± 6.0% (C2S2M2L2), 40.7 ± 5.2% (C2S2M2), and 29.1 ± 3.7% (C2S2) of the membrane surface area.
source: Supercomplex models of different sizes occupied 47.3 ± 6.0% (C2S2M2L2), 40.7 ± 5.2% (C2S2M2), and 29.1 ± 3.7% (C2S2) of the membrane surface area (Figure 4E), with cytb6f occupying an additional 5.8 ± 1.6%.
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative modeling analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Thylakoids are ~70% protein.
source: Thylakoids are ~70% protein (Kirchhoff et al., 2002), suggesting that other complexes such as extra LHCII antennas may occupy up to 20% of the surface area.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The spacing should allow room for rapid diffusion of plastoquinone between PSII and cytb6f within appressed membranes.
source: This spacing should also allow room for rapid diffusion of plastoquinone between PSII and cytb6f within appressed membranes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed spacing between complexes.

claim: The authors observed very little overlap of PSII between adjacent membranes.
source: The membranogram overlays showed very little overlap of PSII between adjacent membranes.
evidence: This claim is based on membranogram overlay analysis.

claim: PSII complexes were almost completely interdigitated across the thylakoid lumen, with only ~4% overlap of EM density.
source: In particular, PSII complexes were almost completely interdigitated across the thylakoid lumen, with only ~4% overlap of EM density (Figure 4B and F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative analysis of membranogram overlays shown in the figures.

claim: PSII interdigitation has previously been predicted from spinach thylakoids with a contracted ~4.5 nm lumen, which sterically could only permit interdigitation.
source: PSII interdigitation has previously been predicted from spinach thylakoids with a contracted ~4.5 nm lumen, which sterically could only permit interdigitation (Daum et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The thylakoids in light-adapted Chlamydomonas cells have a ~9 nm lumen.
source: However, the thylakoids in our light-adapted Chlamydomonas cells have a ~9 nm lumen, which is enough space to permit face-to-face interactions of PSII across the lumen, yet the PSII complexes remain interdigitated.
evidence: This is a measurement from the tomographic data.

claim: Interdigitation could facilitate diffusion of the soluble electron carrier plastocyanin through the lumen, while also enabling the lumen to contract and block diffusion in response to changing light conditions.
source: It has been suggested that interdigitation could facilitate diffusion of the soluble electron carrier plastocyanin through the lumen, while also enabling the lumen to contract and block diffusion in response to changing light conditions (Kirchhoff et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from cited literature.

claim: The overlap of PSII-to-PSII and LHCII-to-LHCII were both statistically indistinguishable from random.
source: To investigate interactions across the stromal gap, we measured the intermembrane overlap from the membrane models of C2S2M2L2-type supercomplexes and compared it to simulated data where the same number of supercomplexes were randomly positioned (Figure 4D and F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2). We found that the overlap of PSII-to-PSII and LHCII-to-LHCII were both statistically indistinguishable from random.
evidence: This claim is based on statistical comparison between experimental and simulated data.

claim: In situ cryo-ET has enabled visualization of the native architecture of thylakoids with molecular resolution.
source: In situ cryo-ET has enabled us to visualize the native architecture of thylakoids with molecular resolution, revealing several striking findings that raise questions about how thylakoids partition their proteins and form appressed stacks.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the capabilities demonstrated in the study.

claim: The authors observe sharp boundaries between PSII and PSI that are tightly coupled to membrane architecture, with no evidence of intermixing at transitions between appressed and non-appressed membrane domains.
source: We observe sharp boundaries between PSII and PSI that are tightly coupled to membrane architecture, with no evidence of intermixing at transitions between appressed and non-appressed membrane domains.
evidence: This is a summary of the key finding from the membranogram analysis.

claim: This argues against the presence of 'grana margins'.
source: This argues against the presence of 'grana margins'.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the absence of observed intermixing.

claim: More definitive conclusions about grana margins will require investigation of the true grana stacks found in higher plants.
source: However, more definitive conclusions will require investigation of the true grana stacks found in higher plants.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the current study.

claim: Semi-crystalline arrays of PSII have been reported in thylakoids isolated from spinach, pea, and diatoms.
source: Semi-crystalline arrays of PSII have been reported in thylakoids isolated from spinach, pea, and diatoms (Staehelin, 1976; Boekema et al., 2000; Daum et al., 2010; Sznee et al., 2011; Goral et al., 2012; Kouřil et al., 2012; Levitan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Randomly arranged PSII has been observed even more frequently than semi-crystalline arrays.
source: However, randomly arranged PSII has been observed even more frequently (Goodenough and Staehelin, 1971; Staehelin, 1976; Olive et al., 1979; Wollman et al., 1980; Daum et al., 2010; Kouřil et al., 2011; Goral et al., 2012; Johnson et al., 2014; Wood et al., 2018; Levitan et al., 2019), and thus the physiological relevance of PSII arrays remains debated (Tsvetkova et al., 1995; Ruban and Johnson, 2015; Tietz et al., 2015; Charuvi et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: PSII complexes are randomly oriented within the appressed thylakoids of Chlamydomonas.
source: In our first look at PSII organization within native membranes, we found that PSII complexes are randomly oriented within the appressed thylakoids of Chlamydomonas, with ample spacing to accommodate C2S2M2-type and C2S2M2L2-type supercomplexes.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the membranogram analysis.

claim: This observation supports the physiological relevance of C2S2M2-type and C2S2M2L2-type supercomplexes.
source: This observation supports the physiological relevance of these larger supercomplexes, which have been primarily characterized in vitro (Caffarri et al., 2009; Su et al., 2017; van Bezouwen et al., 2017; Burton-Smith et al., 2019; Shen et al., 2019; Sheng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed spacing that can accommodate these supercomplexes.

claim: It remains to be proven whether semi-crystalline PSII arrays form inside the native cellular environment or whether they are a consequence of isolating thylakoid membranes.
source: However, it remains to be proven whether semi-crystalline PSII arrays form inside the native cellular environment or whether they are a consequence of isolating thylakoid membranes.
evidence: This is a statement about an unresolved question in the field.

claim: The authors determined that PSII supercomplexes randomly overlap between appressed membranes.
source: Unlike earlier techniques, our combination of in situ cryo-ET with membranograms has enabled us to visualize the organization of PSII across multiple adjacent stacked thylakoids within native cells. We determined that PSII supercomplexes randomly overlap between appressed membranes, challenging the idea that thylakoid stacking is mediated by specific static interactions between LHCII or PSII proteins across the stromal gap.
evidence: This claim is based on the statistical analysis comparing experimental and random overlap.

claim: Random overlap of PSII supercomplexes challenges the idea that thylakoid stacking is mediated by specific static interactions between LHCII or PSII proteins across the stromal gap.
source: We determined that PSII supercomplexes randomly overlap between appressed membranes, challenging the idea that thylakoid stacking is mediated by specific static interactions between LHCII or PSII proteins across the stromal gap.
evidence: This is an inference based on the finding of random overlap.

claim: The study establishes the methodological foundation to explore the conservation of thylakoid molecular architecture with other ecologically important phototrophs.
source: Beyond these observations, our study establishes the methodological foundation to explore the conservation of thylakoid molecular architecture with other ecologically important phototrophs and dissect the mechanisms that adapt this architecture to changing environmental conditions.
evidence: This is a statement about the broader implications of the methodological advances.

claim: The mat3-4 strain has smaller cells that vitrify better by plunge freezing.
source: The mat3-4 strain has smaller cells that vitrify better by plunge freezing.
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of the strain used.

claim: Comparative 77K fluorescence measurements showed that mat3-4 and wild-type cells had similar spectra under the conditions that the cells were grown and frozen onto EM grids.
source: Comparative 77K fluorescence measurements showed that mat3-4 and wild-type cells had similar spectra under the conditions that the cells were grown and frozen onto EM grids (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by 77K fluorescence data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Cells were grown to mid-log phase (1000–2000 cells/μL) in TAP medium under constant light conditions (~90 µmol photons m−2s−1) and bubbling with normal air.
source: For cryo-ET, mat3-4 cells were grown to mid-log phase (1000–2000 cells/μL) in Tris-acetate-phosphate (TAP) medium under constant light conditions (~90 µmol photons m−2s−1) and bubbling with normal air.
evidence: This describes the experimental growth conditions.

claim: Cryo-FIB milling was performed using a Quanta dual-beam FIB/SEM instrument equipped with a Quorum PP3010 preparation chamber.

source: Each tomogram was acquired from a separate cell and thus is both a biological and technical replicate.
